 ‘Put All the Pressure on Me, I Don’t Care!’ — Eric Chelle Defends Super Eagles Selection, Sends Strong Warning to Players Ahead of Tanzania Return Leg
 By Lovette Ochicha - November 17, 2026 
 Facebook Twitter Pinterest WhatsApp 
 Super Eagles head coach Eric Sekou Chelle has defended his tactical decisions and team selection, declaring that he will not bow to external pressure over how Nigeria should play as the team prepares to face Tanzania in Tuesday’s crucial 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying return fixture in Zanzibar, Sports247.ng reports.
 Chelle’s comments come after Nigeria defeated the Taifa Stars 3-1 in Uyo on Friday, with the Franco-Malian tactician insisting that his decisions are guided by tactical requirements, available players and the opposition.
 “Me, I have to take my decision. I take my responsibility. I do my choice,” Chelle declared.
 “Even if I want to play in 4-4-2 diamond, I will play in 4-4-2 diamond. You can put the pressure on me like you want, I don’t care.”
 The Super Eagles coach stressed that his preferred formation is not fixed, explaining that he could equally deploy a flat 4-4-2 depending on the circumstances.
 “It depends on the philosophy, depends on the players that we have, it depends on the team against which we play, and I try to find the best way,” he explained.
 Chelle also revealed that preparations for Tanzania began well before the opening encounter, dismissing suggestions that his decisions were based merely on instinct.
 “We prepared the game against Tanzania during two or three months before the game,” he disclosed.
 Turning his attention to player selection, Chelle warned that representing Nigeria requires consistent performances rather than relying on reputation or previous achievements.
 “Sometimes you have to send a message to the player who usually plays: ‘My guy, you have not arrived. You have to continue to do your job,'” he stated.
 The coach emphasised that his responsibility is to identify the best available players while ensuring every member of the squad remains motivated.
 “Everybody needs to be every time, at the best moment, the best player on the pitch,” he said.
 Despite acknowledging that some players occasionally struggle, Chelle defended their commitment to the national team
 “I can tell you that these guys, they give everything for this jersey,” he insisted.
 Nigeria enter Tuesday’s return fixture seeking another victory to strengthen their qualification prospects after moving to six points in Group L.
 For Chelle, the message is unmistakable: he will accept responsibility for his decisions, demand consistent performances and defend players who demonstrate commitment to the Super Eagles jersey.
